entries.claim: The new parent lstat is still a time-of-check/time-of-use guard, so it does not close the symlink escape against a concurrent filesystem change.
entries.failure_scenario: When `deferred/` is absent (or is an empty real directory), `lstatSync(carryRoot)` observes it as safe. Before the later recursive `mkdirSync(dest)` runs, another process replaces or creates `deferred` as a symlink to an outside directory. `mkdirSync` follows that intermediate symlink and creates `<outside>/<phase>`, after which the existing `renameSync` moves committed DEFERRED members outside the planning tree. The check and creation need an operation resistant to replacement, not only a prior lstat.

counter_evidence.note: The race is real and the severity is not. What round one closed was reachable with NO extra privilege: a symlink committed on a branch arrives through an ordinary git checkout, and the carry followed it. This residual needs a concurrent process that already holds write access to .planning/ - and an adversary with that access can delete or move the very members the race aims to relocate, so the escape crosses no boundary it was not already on the far side of. Nor is the demanded remedy available here: an atomic answer needs openat/O_NOFOLLOW-style operations Node's fs surface does not expose, so 'an operation resistant to replacement' names no call this runtime has. Held as an open item, not a blocker.
